newsitem.title: ESTONIA: REPORT SAYS HOIU, TALLINNA STARTED MERGER TALKS.
newsitem.headline: REPORT SAYS HOIU, TALLINNA STARTED MERGER TALKS.

text.p: Aripaev newspaper said on Friday that Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank have started merger negotiations, although the banks said there have been no official meetings.
Aripaev, quoting its own sources, said that Hoiupank's owners have given the bank chairman Olari Taal authority to held merger talks with Tallinna Pank.
But Hoiupank deputy chairman Priit Haller told the newspaper that the bank has not started official negotiatons with Tallinna Pank.
Tallinna Pank council chairman Guido Sammelselg told the newspaper that the talks were "between friends".
Sammelselg added that he would agree to sell his stake in Tallinna Pank if a favourable offer was made. Sammelselg owns 7-8 percent of the bank, the newspaper said.
Haller said that a possible merger with Tallinna Pank would add to Hoiupank's effectiveness and labor resources.
"The merger would be made only when such a synergy is gained," he was quoted as saying by the newspaper.
Hoiupank has said earlier it mulling a merger to gain market share and that it was most interested in Forekspank and Tallinna Pank.
A Hoiupank spokesperson told Reuters that the bank will respond to the article with a statement before the bourse opening.
